data.why: The training nodes have no internet and no cross-node filesystem: preprocess_public_data.py downloads the raw MovieLens archive with urlretrieve, and get_reco_dataset() then reads tmp/<prefix>/sasrec_format.csv relative to the job's cwd. The prepared file therefore has to travel inside the job package (or as its own gcs:// package), produced once on a machine that does have network access. A job whose package lacks it fails as a `data` failure in the loader, which is the safe failure: it never reports a number.

note: How this domain is measured: the repository's own entry point, with the frozen ML-1M config, wrapped by run-metrics.py, which is the only piece that turns the training log into the metric contract's number. Three things are load-bearing. (1) `cwd` is the candidate's worktree, so run-metrics.py must live at the root of the checkout `runner.repo` points at — copy it there from this pack, or commit it to the fork; the pack cannot reach into the worktree any other way. (2) `{free_port}` becomes a free port at run time: two jobs on one node otherwise collide on main.py's `--master_port`, and the cluster does not isolate cards between jobs (see the ticket-14 notes). (3) The metric is the last *full* eval epoch, never a truncated one and never a tensorboard average; that rule lives in the metric contract's `window` and is implemented in run-metrics.py. Nothing here downloads anything: the dataset is prepared before packaging.
